MiGDL Pipeline
Lineage

Column-level lineage for the whole path a student record travels: from the Ed-Fi API, through Silver, Gold and Platinum, out to the REST endpoints MAISA's apps consume. Read-only — no draw.io, no Miro, no account. Click any column to trace it end to end.

20views — overview, 18 domains, the API
146gold / platinum / temp tables
403bronze tables, 81 ingested
19REST endpoints
793API response fields
7,112lineage edges, deduplicated

How to read it

Layers flow left to right

Every view is the same six lanes. A domain only shows the lanes it uses.

LaneWhat is in it
BRONZE The landed Ed-Fi API resources, one flat table per resource, every column varchar. Read from an Athena information_schema export, so these are real columns rather than a placeholder. Columns struck through are not carried into Silver.
SILVER Flattened API resources, per district (silversd<N> schemas; district_sd1 shown as canonical). Parent tables end _p0, children _c1, grandchildren _c2.
GOLD conf gold.* conformed tables. Loaded from goldstage.staging_*, which is column-identical (SCD2 merge), so staging and conf are drawn as one node.
GOLD star Derived dims and facts — dim_student, fact_student_enrollment, and the rest of the star schema.
TEMP Redshift temp / staging tables used mid-flight.
PLATINUM Curated marts — MiRead, EWIMS, rosters, curated_* extracts.
API The 19 REST endpoints of maisa-consumption-api, the layer MAISA's apps actually see. Columns on these cards are response fields, named as the JSON delivers them (schools[].sections[].teacher.first_name).

Edges

LineMeaning
bronze → silver, carried The column name is identical on both sides — 1,131 of them.
bronze → silver, flattened A Bronze reference or nested object becomes prefixed Silver columns: schoolreference → schoolreferenceschoolid, ext → extmimedicalnotes. 532 of them.
bronze → silver, collection A Bronze array column is promoted to its own child table: identificationdocuments → edfi_student_identificationdocuments_c1. Table-level, since the array's interior is not described by the schema export.
silver → gold conf Column rename / flatten. Ed-Fi JSON path names pick up underscores — calendarreferencecalendarcode becomes calendarreference_calendarcode.
gold conf → derived Real transformation: joins, descriptor splitting, key derivation.
→ platinum Curation into a mart.
→ API response field A gold or platinum column served directly as a response field.
→ API, packed in JSON The column is aggregated into a JSON/SUPER column (JSON_SERIALIZE, or a hand-built JSON string) that the Lambda unpacks into nested response objects.
dashed grey Table-level edge where no single-column mapping exists — flag columns set by WHERE EXISTS(...) predicates, and the bronze → silver flatten.

Tracing is no longer bounded by the view. Lineage is held as one graph, so a trace runs the whole pipeline in both directions however you got there. Anything one hop away that the current view does not contain is pulled in as a card marked one hop upstream or one hop downstream, and dropped again on the next selection. Clicking a row in the panel that belongs to another view switches to the view that owns it and selects it there.

Columns with nothing downstream are marked. In any view, a column that feeds nothing anywhere in the pipeline gets a hollow dot. Bronze columns that never reach Silver stay struck through instead. Endpoints are excluded — the API is the end of the line by definition, so every response field would otherwise be flagged.

Where a column is a literal or a derivation, the inspector shows it. Select gold.dim_student.is_special_education and the panel prints FALSE — the column has no upstream because it is hard-coded. Audit columns show GETDATE(), and derived keys show the expression that mints them.

The overview says where everything lives. In 00 · Overview every card carries a blue badge naming the domain view that owns it — 07 course-section, 13 programs, and so on. Click the badge to open that view. It is the fastest way to answer "which diagram is this table in?" without reading the domain list.

Endpoints appear in every domain they read. The 19 REST endpoints are drawn in full in view 19 · Consumption API, and again as faded reference cards inside each domain whose tables they consume — carrying only the fields sourced from that domain. So a Gold column now shows you which apps would notice if it changed.

Dashed, faded table cards are references owned by another view (for example dim_student appearing inside the discipline mart). Only the referenced columns are listed on them — open that table's own domain to see it in full.

How the lineage was derived

bronze → silver is derived by name from an Athena information_schema export of the Bronze database (403 tables, 10,329 columns) against the Silver schemas. Every one of the 1,663 real Silver parent columns resolves to a Bronze column — 1,131 by identical name, 532 by prefix where a reference or nested object was flattened. The remaining 305 Silver columns (lakeid, currentflag, effectivefrom and the rest) are added by the ingestion and have no Bronze source, which is why they are drawn with none.

Ten Bronze columns per resource never reach Silver, the same ten every time: changeversion, keyvalues, oldkeyvalues, newkeyvalues, recordflag, typeofdata, edfiversion, datastandard, upload_date and schooldistrictid (Silver keeps schooldistrict instead). They are ingestion and change-capture metadata, not payload — but note that changeversion and the keyvalue triplet are Ed-Fi's own change-tracking fields, so anything downstream that wants incremental sync would have to go back to Bronze for them.

goldstage → gold conf → derived → platinum is parsed from the actual ETL SQL (etl/edfi_gold_platinum/sql/**) and manifests with sqlglot, at column level, including the UPDATE-based enrichment passes (dim_student_2..16.sql and friends).

silver → goldstage is the one hop still reconstructed rather than read. The authoritative column-mapping JSON lives only in S3 (bronze/silver_to_gold_mapping/), not in the repo. Conf columns are matched to silver columns by stripped name within an entity family.

Match confidence is shown on every conf table. Across the 81 conf tables, 67 matched every column (1.00), 13 scored 0.90–0.99, and 1 scored 0.80–0.89. None fell below 0.80. Unmatched columns are generally derived (surrogate keys, audit columns) rather than missing — but treat a sub-1.00 table as indicative rather than authoritative until the S3 mapping is checked.

platinum.curated_ewims_student_early_warn_incidents_actions is built by PySpark (core/ewims_curated.py), not SQL, so it carries table-level edges only.

Two tables are named for the opposite of what they hold

fact_student_section_enrollment_conf holds attendance events. It actually contains edfi_studentSectionAttendanceEvent rows — its INSERT column list is attendanceeventcategorydescriptor, eventdate, arrivaltime, departuretime and so on, with no enrollment columns at all. It is placed in 12 · Attendance.

fact_student_section_grade_conf holds section enrollments. It actually contains edfi_studentSectionAssociation rows — begindate, enddate, attemptstatusdescriptor, homeroomindicator — and no grade columns whatsoever. Real grades live in fact_grade_conf. It is placed in 07 · Courses & Sections.

The repo knows: fact_student_enrollment.sql aliases the ..._grade_conf table as enr and the ..._enrollment_conf table as enr_att. The derived-layer logic is correct today — this is a comprehension and maintenance hazard, not a live data bug. Both views place these tables by their contents, not their names.

Consumption API

What the apps actually receive

View 19 covers maisa-consumption-api — the REST layer MiEWIMS, MiRead, MiSAFEStudent and Community Schools Manager call instead of querying MiDX directly.

The 19 endpoints are read from the OpenAPI spec (api-2_2_2.yaml, v2.2.2) for the response contract, and from the handlers' own SQL for what feeds it. The SQL is not reconstructed from templates — each handler's query builder is executed with a synthetic request, so the query recorded here is the one the Lambda issues.

791 of 793 response fields trace to a specific gold or platinum column. The remaining two are computed in the SELECT with no single source column. 78 fields arrive packed inside a JSON column — the query aggregates them with JSON_SERIALIZE or a hand-built JSON string and the Lambda unpacks them into nested objects; those are drawn with a finer dash and attributed to the column that carries them.

The API reads 23 tables — 15 Gold, 8 Platinum. One of them, gold.dim_school, is joined but serves no response field; it is drawn with a table-level edge only. Everything else in Gold and Platinum is, as far as this repo shows, not reachable through the API.
